Mina (eng-infra): heads up — saw the dedicated-eu gpu pool hit sustained saturation for ~6m during the deploy window. latency spiked and a bunch of small chat requests timed out. any quick tuning ideas for our TPM/RPM admission that won't blow cost? :grimacing:
AJ (eng-sre): ouch. did we get a breakdown by model/seq-length?
Mina (eng-infra): yep, mostly short chats to the 'small-chat-v2' variant. median seq ~60 tokens. GPUs were at 98% mem and 92% util.
Kai (eng-runtime): short seqs are awful for throughput unless batching kicks in. looks like batch_wait was at 5ms but arrival variance prevented good packing.
Eve (eng-infra): do we have per-gpu token-rate estimates? we used a naive 30k tokens/min/GPU when provisioning last quarter. might be off after the quantized model changes.
AJ (eng-sre): i pulled the perf matrix — on EU-g4 with current build: 45k tokens/min/GPU for seq=60 with batching ideal. but effective tokens/min drops to ~22k if batching efficiency < 50%.
Mina (eng-infra): so our admission math that says pool_tpm = gpus * 30k is optimistic in that scenario. we should account for observed batching efficiency. can we compute a more robust policy?
Kai (eng-runtime): propose: observed_tpm_per_gpu = theoretical_tpm * batching_efficiency_ewma. then pool_tpm = sum_gpus observed_tpm_per_gpu * safety_factor. and allow a small burst pool based on spare memory headroom.
Eve (eng-infra): love that. concrete formula suggestion (pseudo):
```
# theoretical tokens per minute per GPU at seq L
theoretical_tpm = tokens_per_sec_at_L * 60
batch_eff = EWMA(batch_fill_fraction, alpha=0.2)
observed_tpm = theoretical_tpm * batch_eff
pool_tpm = floor(sum_over_gpus(observed_tpm) * 0.85)  # 15% safety margin
burst_credits = floor(sum_over_gpus(max_memory_free / gpu_mem * observed_tpm) * 0.1)
admission_rate = pool_tpm + burst_credits
```
AJ (eng-sre): that burst_credits calc is neat — ties burst to memory headroom rather than an arbitrary token bucket. should cap bursts per-customer to avoid noisy neighbors.
Mina (eng-infra): agree. per-customer cap = min(customer_configured_cap, per_gpu_share * burst_quota). we also need a decay window so burst credits don't persist after sustained load.
Kai (eng-runtime): implement decaying burst via a leaky bucket: grant credits that decay exponentially with half-life e.g., 3m. simpler than manual timers.
InfraBot: [metric alert] eu-dedicated-gpu-pool_utilization > 0.9 for 7m (since 1842561000)
AJ (eng-sre): note on TPM vs RPM — we should publish both. TPM controls tokens per minute; RPM controls request count rate. for short-chat-heavy traffic, RPM is the limiting factor, not TPM. we saw request spikes at ~1200 rpm causing queueing.
Eve (eng-infra): good call. add an RPM gating layer that looks at effective tokens per request (avg_tokens) and enforces: allowed_rpm = floor(pool_tpm / avg_tokens_per_request). this prevents token exhaustion surprises.
Mina (eng-infra): example numbers: pool_tpm=900k, avg_tokens=60 => allowed_rpm = 15k. in our incident pool_tpm was ~540k (using old 30k/gpu), avg_tokens 45 => allowed_rpm=12k but arrival was 20k rpm — mismatch.
Kai (eng-runtime): we'll need realtime avg_tokens EWMA per route to adjust allowed_rpm dynamically. pushing that to routing can enable graceful degradation per-route.
AJ (eng-sre): operational knobs: 1) alpha for EWMA 2) safety_factor 3) burst_half_life 4) per-customer burst caps. default sensible values? maybe alpha=0.15, safety=0.82, burst_half_life=180s.
Eve (eng-infra): let's run a short sim on historical traffic and compute expected drop rate for those defaults. I'll sketch a small sim in python and post results.
Mina (eng-infra): also add a cheap heuristic: when GPU mem util > 95% for >60s, force batch_wait down to 1ms to prioritize latency over throughput. might avoid longer queuing.
Kai (eng-runtime): careful — dropping batch_wait drastically increases small-request tail latencies for others. but as emergency measure it's fine if it's opt-in per-pool. mark as kill-switch.
AJ (eng-sre): followups: Eve — sim + summary in this thread. Kai — PR for admission controller changes with hooks for EWMA metrics. Mina — update runbook to include burst decay and emergency batch_wait toggle. I'll coordinate change windows. :thumbsup:
Eve (eng-infra): starting sim now, will post a short table of expected vs observed saturation in ~10m.
Mina (eng-infra): thanks all. tagging @oncall for visibility.
Kai (eng-runtime): one more micro-optimization: use hist-based token-per-request estimate (p90) when enforcing RPM during spikes to be conservative. reduces slam. :thinking:
AJ (eng-sre): agreed. let's keep the nominal to mean but switch to p90 for enforcement windows.
Mina (eng-infra): perfect. logging: include admission decisions in trace headers so we can backfill why requests were throttled.
InfraBot: [deploy-bot] PR #4982 deployed to canary at 1842561500
Eve (eng-infra): sim results (quick): with defaults alpha=0.15, safety=0.82, burst_half_life=180s on last week's traffic — predicted saturations reduced from 6 -> 1 per day and peak drops from 12% to 4%. pushing full report in ~20m.
Mina (eng-infra): excellent. schedule a short rollout to canary pool tomorrow. good discussion. :rocket:
